adjudication_records.issue_text: Predicate change in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() silently drops org-linked non-public IDPs from all getForLogin results, removing private org brokers from the org's own login page (behavioral regression beyond caching)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This predicate is used to qualify IDPs returned by `getForLogin(...)` (see static import `getLoginPredicate` and usage in new cache invalidation logic). Because the condition is unconditional (not dependent on `FetchMode` or the `organizationId` argument), any IDP linked to an organization (`getOrganizationId() != null`) will be excluded unless it is marked `BROKER_PUBLIC`. That means org-linked non-public (private) brokers will never appear in `getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, orgId)` or `getForLogin(ALL, orgId)`, which is consistent with the finding’s claim of a behavioral regression beyond caching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test masks the regression because every test IDP linked to an org has BROKER_PUBLIC=true

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, every IDP that gets linked to the organization is created in the `for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++)` loop with `if (i >= 10) idpRep.getConfig().put(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, "true")`, and then only `i = 10..19` are linked to the org. So the test never exercises org-linked IDPs where `BROKER_PUBLIC` is absent/false, despite the diff changing `getLoginPredicate()` to require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC == true`. This is a concrete coverage gap in the added test; calling it a ‘masked regression’ is speculative, but the underlying issue (test only covers public org-linked IDPs) is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organization link/unlink through OrganizationProvider may bypass login-cache invalidation, leaving stale getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, orgId) caches after org admins link/unlink a broker

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching for `getForLogin()` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` keyed only by realm+`FetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), with org-specific results stored inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` under `searchKey` (orgId). Invalidation of these caches is only registered on IDP `create`, `update` (via `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`), and `remove`. The diff shows no invalidation hook tied to organization link/unlink operations themselves (which likely happen via `OrganizationProvider`/`organizations().identityProviders().addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider`). If those operations can change which IDPs appear for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` without going through IDP update/remove, the new caches could become stale. The diff doesn’t prove whether link/unlink triggers an IDP update internally, so it’s a concrete potential gap but not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup uses getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) with wrong alias "alias", causing NPE at cleanup-registration time and leaking 20+ test IDPs into the shared test realm

remove() always hits the delegate even on the cached fast path, performing an unnecessary delegate lookup; if the delegate returns null while a cached entry exists, login-cache invalidation is skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now unconditionally does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking the cache, so even the cached fast-path pays for a delegate lookup (performance/regression vs prior behavior). It’s also true that if `storedIdp` is `null`, `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` will not invalidate login caches because the login predicate is `Objects::nonNull`-guarded. However, the new `getForLogin()` implementation detects missing IDPs (`getById(id) == null`) and then invalidates the login cache key and falls back to the delegate, so this skipped invalidation does not clearly produce incorrect results from the diff alone; it’s mainly inefficiency/edge-case cache hygiene.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() may be null (lazily initialized), causing NPE in getLoginPredicate().test(idp), including in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidation*

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to call `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without any null-guard on `getConfig()`. If `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can ever return null, this new predicate will throw an NPE anywhere it’s evaluated (including the newly added `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` paths that call `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`). The diff itself doesn’t prove `getConfig()` can be null, but it does introduce an unguarded dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Baking BROKER_PUBLIC filter into the shared getLoginPredicate changes org IDP login semantics: org-private brokers are excluded from getForLogin(ALL, orgId)/ORG_ONLY results even in org context where they should be shown to org members

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to include `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This is a context-free predicate (it does not take the `organizationId` argument of `getForLogin` into account), so any IDP linked to an organization (`getOrganizationId() != null`) but not marked `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` will no longer satisfy the shared “login” predicate. Since `getForLogin(...)` is the API used to list login-available IDPs (e.g., in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`), this change can exclude org-linked but non-public brokers even when calling `getForLogin(ALL, orgId)` / `ORG_ONLY`, matching the finding’s stated semantic regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models without createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, while cache-miss/invalid paths return org-aware wrapped models, causing inconsistent results

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)`, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path builds a `Set<IdentityProviderModel>` by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and then returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This is a diff-verifiable inconsistency in returned model wrapping between cache-hit vs cache-miss paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent revision handling in org-specific cache searches: first population uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) but subsequent branch uses cache.getCurrentCounter() after invalidation, risking dropped or stale org-specific sub-results under concurrency

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin() caching logic, the revision passed to cache.addRevisioned(...) is inconsistent between branches: when query == null it uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), but when a query exists and a new org-specific sub-result is added after cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), it uses cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). This inconsistency is visible in the diff and could be a real concurrency/consistency concern (which revision should govern the entry), but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes dropped/stale results at runtime without knowing RealmCacheManager’s revision semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup bug in OrganizationCacheTest uses literal "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i (also for idp-20 creation), causing cleanups to fail and intended cleanup coverage never runs

Unbounded growth of the login cache entry in getForLogin: single IdentityProviderListQuery accumulates a search-result set per organizationId with no bound on distinct search keys, causing unbounded accumulation in the shared Infinispan cache

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the cache key is only (realmId + ".idp.login." + fetchMode), i.e., it does not include organizationId. The code then stores results per "searchKey" (organizationId or "") inside a single cached IdentityProviderListQuery (query.getIDPs(searchKey)). When a new organizationId is queried and not present (cached == null), it creates a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query) passing the previous query, which strongly implies it retains/merges prior per-searchKey results. There is no bound or eviction of distinct searchKey entries, so over time the single cached object can grow with every distinct organizationId requested, defeating cache entry limits and risking unbounded memory growth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached path in getForLogin skips createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, causing cache hit and miss paths to return different results for the same query

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results with `map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cached path builds results by iterating cached IDs and returning `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` directly with no explicit wrapping. From the diff alone, this is a concrete inconsistency between miss and hit paths. Whether it actually causes different returned models depends on how `getById` is implemented (not shown in the diff); if `getById` already applies the organization-aware wrapping, then results would still match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible NPE in getLoginPredicate() when org-linked IDPs have a null config map, as getConfig() is dereferenced unconditionally when organizationId != null

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` clause `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null-check when `getOrganizationId() != null`. If `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can ever be null (not shown in the diff), this would NPE. The diff alone doesn’t prove `getConfig()` may be null, so it’s a robustness/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect from this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalidations from organization-side IDP mutations may bypass the update hook, causing login caches to serve stale lists when IDP models are mutated through paths not going through update()

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds login-list caching in `getForLogin(...)` and explicitly registers invalidation on the IDP storage provider’s `create`, `update` (including organizationId-change detection), and `remove` paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). The finding claims org-side mutations bypass `update()` and thus leave stale login caches, but the diff does not show any organization-side mutation path that updates an IDP without going through `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update()`. In fact, the newly added test (`testCacheIDPForLogin`, step 4) performs an organization link operation (`addIdentityProvider`) and asserts that the login caches are cleared, suggesting the intended org-linking flow does invalidate (or triggers an update) rather than bypass it. Therefore the alleged bypass is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached path materializes the full result set in a HashSet, destroying delegate-defined ordering so cached and uncached paths can return IDPs in different order

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached implementation of `getForLogin(...)`, results are cached as a `Set` (`collect(Collectors.toSet())` into `cached`, and later stored/retrieved via `IdentityProviderListQuery`), then materialized into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` and returned as `identityProviders.stream()`. This loses any ordering the delegate stream might have had, while the uncached path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` directly (preserving its encounter order). The diff doesn’t show a contract requiring a stable order, so this is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency risk rather than a provable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Result-set materialization is unbounded: getForLogin caches all qualifying internal IDs per realm/org per mode, with cluster-wide replication amplifying large cache entries for big realms

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` implementation in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` materializes the full result set into a `Set<String>` of internal IDs (`collect(Collectors.toSet())`) and stores it in an `IdentityProviderListQuery` cache entry keyed by realm + mode, with per-`organizationId` variants stored inside the same cached query object. There is no `first/max` bounding or size limit, so for realms with many qualifying IDPs this can create large cache entries, and (given Infinispan’s typical clustered replication/invalidation behavior) can amplify memory/traffic cluster-wide. This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/architecture concern, not a correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses literal alias "alias" instead of the actual created aliases ("idp-alias-" + i and "idp-alias-20"), making cleanup a no-op and leaking 20+ IDPs into the realm, breaking other tests and re-runs

adjudication.rationale: In testCacheIDPForLogin, after creating each IDP with alias "idp-alias-" + i (and later "idp-alias-20"), the cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (literal string "alias"). This does not match any of the created aliases, so cleanup is effectively a no-op and can leak the created IDPs into the realm, potentially impacting other tests/reruns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() invalidation of a login IDP is never tested — only a disabled IDP is removed, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation path and the isInvalid(cacheKey) path with storedIdp from the delegate are unexercised

adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove(String alias)` implementation, it always fetches `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which only invalidates login caches when `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only removes `idp-alias-1`, which is created with `setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)` and therefore is disabled (i=1) and does not qualify as a login IDP, so the `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` invalidation branch for a login IDP is not exercised. The test also doesn’t set up conditions to drive the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey)) { registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp); ... }` branch for the alias cache key in `remove()`, so that path remains untested too.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No verification that a second getForLogin call (cache hit path) returns the correct set of IdentityProviderModel objects, nor how createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping behaves on the cache-hit path vs. the invalid path

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` caching logic has two distinct return paths: on cache-miss/invalid it returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (wrapped models), but on cache-hit it reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly without `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (see `getForLogin` loop). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only asserts cache entries exist/are invalidated and counts stored in `IdentityProviderListQuery`; it never makes a *second* `getForLogin` call and asserts the actual returned `IdentityProviderModel` set or whether wrapping differs between cache-hit vs invalid paths. This is a concrete missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The "new searchKey" branch in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin uses cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial branch uses startupRevision; no test exercises caching multiple organizationId search keys under the same FetchMode cache key

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin, when query == null it caches with cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), but when query exists and cached==null (new searchKey under same cacheKey) it invalidates and then caches with cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). This inconsistency is present in the diff, but whether it’s incorrect can’t be proven from the diff alone. The added test testCacheIDPForLogin only populates one searchKey per FetchMode cache key ("" for REALM_ONLY; orgaId for ORG_ONLY and ALL), so the cached==null/new-searchKey branch is not exercised, which is a concrete test gap for newly added caching logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit test for getLoginPredicate covering null config (which would NPE for org-linked IDPs), org-linked public, org-linked non-public, and non-org IDPs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that dereferences `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null`. This introduces new behavior (and a potential NPE if `getConfig()` can be null), but the added test (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) focuses on caching and does not explicitly cover `getLoginPredicate` edge cases like null config or an org-linked non-public IDP (BROKER_PUBLIC missing/false).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new idp.isEnabled() re-filter in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean is untested — no test verifies a disabled-but-org-public IDP doesn't appear on the login page after being served through the cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `idp.isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)` (both branches) to guard against “idp might have been wrapped.” The newly added `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()` exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and cache invalidation/results, but it does not invoke `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` or validate the login-page list rendering path. So the specific UI-layer re-filter behavior (e.g., ensuring a disabled-but-org-public IDP never appears after cached/wrapped retrieval) is not directly tested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update() path where an IDP's alias changes is not tested for the login caches, so whether cached internalId-based lists remain correct when invalidation is skipped is unverified

adjudication.rationale: The new login-cache invalidation logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.update()` calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)`, which only considers login predicate changes and `organizationId` changes (and explicitly may skip invalidation). The added `testCacheIDPForLogin()` exercises hideOnLogin/public/org-link scenarios, but does not cover an update where the IDP alias changes. While the login cache stores internalIds (`IdentityProviderModel::getInternalId`) and may remain correct, this specific update path’s interaction with “skipped invalidation” is not verified by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate() semantic change leaks beyond caching layer: cache-driven optimization altered shared SPI predicate affecting all implementations and callers (coupling/Separation of Concerns)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` in the shared SPI (`server-spi/.../IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`) by adding an extra constraint: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This is a semantic change that will affect all callers/implementations using `getLoginPredicate()`, not just the new cache invalidation logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` (which now statically imports and relies on `getLoginPredicate()` for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). While not provably a functional bug from the diff alone, it is a legitimate coupling/scope concern because behavior is being altered at the SPI level rather than being confined to the caching layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Excluding non-public org IDPs from getLoginPredicate() globally causes behavior regression: FetchMode.ALL for an organization should return org-scoped members-only brokers, which now disappear from login flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This means any IDP linked to an organization (`organizationId != null`) is excluded from the login predicate unless it is marked `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, regardless of `FetchMode` or whether an `organizationId` is explicitly provided to `getForLogin(...)`. Since `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` uses `getForLogin(ALL, orgId)` when an organization is present, org-linked but non-public (members-only) brokers would no longer be returned and thus would “disappear” from login flows compared to prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE risk in getLoginPredicate(): when getOrganizationId() != null and getConfig() returns null, idp.getConfig().get(...) throws NPE; no guard unlike other predicates

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new clause to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null-check on `getConfig()`. If `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` can ever be null, this would cause an NPE when `getOrganizationId() != null`. The diff itself doesn’t prove whether `getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null, so this is a robustness/defensive-coding concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) in getForLogin() miss branch bypasses startupRevision guard, allowing stale data to silently overwrite concurrent invalidation

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin() implementation, the true cache-miss path (`query == null`) does use `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`. The only place using `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())` is the sub-case where a cache entry exists but the specific `searchKey` is not cached (`cached == null`), and it explicitly calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` before reloading and writing. The diff alone does not show that this “bypasses a startupRevision guard” or that it can overwrite concurrent invalidation; it matches the existing pattern used elsewhere in this class (e.g., list-query caching logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit and cache-miss paths in getForLogin() diverge in model wrapping: miss paths explicitly wrap with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel while hit path relies on implicit re-entry through getById, creating hidden self-coupling and inconsistent output contract
matched_golden_ids: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that getForLogin() calls session.identityProviders().getById() (the cached accessor) instead of the delegate, causing re-entry/recursion through the caching layer. The candidate flags that the cache-hit path relies on implicit re-entry through getById, creating self-coupling and inconsistent behavior—this is the same underlying problem (calling back into the caching layer rather than the delegate).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup uses wrong alias 'alias' which matches none of the created IDPs (idp-alias-0 ... idp-alias-20), making cleanup dead code that NPEs or no-ops and leaves 21 IDPs polluting the realm

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that the test cleanup references the alias string 'alias' instead of the created IDP aliases ('idp-alias-' + i), which is exactly the golden issue about incorrect alias usage in cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate re-derives login predicate components duplicatively and will silently under-invalidate if LoginFilter gains a new dimension, only special-casing organizationId

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` does not “re-derive login predicate components”; it simply calls the centralized `getLoginPredicate()` on the original and updated models and only adds an extra `Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())` check to avoid invalidation when the IDP remains login-eligible and its org link didn’t change. Because it relies on `getLoginPredicate()` (which itself is built from `LoginFilter.values()`), if `LoginFilter` gains a new dimension it will be reflected in the predicate result, and the method will invalidate whenever predicate truth changes. The claim of “silent under-invalidation” due to new `LoginFilter` dimensions is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded cache-key fan-out per organization: single cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) entry accumulates per-organization result sets in one IdentityProviderListQuery, causing repeated invalidateObject/rebuild churn and growing parent chain for realms with many organizations

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the cache key is only realm+mode (cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)) and does not include organizationId. The code stores results keyed by a per-request "searchKey" inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery. When a new organizationId is queried and query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, it calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and rebuilds a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query) chaining the previous query as a parent. This design can cause churn (invalidate/rebuild per new orgId) and potentially unbounded growth of the parent chain / accumulated per-org result sets as more organizations are queried, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern shown by the diff (not a correctness defect per se).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated invalidation loop: registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate both contain identical FetchMode.values() registration loop that will drift; should extract invalidateLoginCaches() helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show duplicated code: both registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate contain the same `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)); }` loop. However, this is a refactoring/DRY suggestion (maintainability/style) rather than a verifiable defect or a concrete, nontrivial review issue introduced by the change; the claim about “will drift” is speculative and not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Magic sentinel empty string for null organizationId in getForLogin cache key searchKey is a subtle contract that will break if a real empty-string orgId or third state is added; should use named constant or explicit key-composition method

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the cache uses `String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` and later indexes cached results via `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` / `getIDPs("")`. This does create an implicit sentinel contract that conflates `null` with the empty string for the organization dimension of the cache. While the diff doesn’t show any current way for a real organizationId to be `""`, the concern is diff-grounded as a maintainability/contract risk in the cache keying logic rather than a demonstrable defect today.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin returns raw models without the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper, while cache-miss paths do wrap them, causing inconsistent login results depending on cache state

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, the cache-miss paths explicitly wrap results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (both the isInvalid(cacheKey) early-return and the fallback when an IDP is missing). However, the cache-hit path reconstructs results via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns identityProviders.stream() without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so callers can receive differently wrapped IdentityProviderModel instances depending on cache state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate now excludes org-linked, non-public IDPs everywhere (shared SPI predicate change), so getForLogin(ALL, orgId) no longer returns non-public org IDPs that should still be available when the organization is resolved — a semantic behavior change smuggled into a caching PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared SPI predicate `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to always require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC == true` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`). That is a semantic change affecting any code path that relies on this predicate (not just the new Infinispan caching). The PR’s new tests only create org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, so they don’t cover/guard behavior for org-linked non-public IDPs when calling `getForLogin(ALL, orgId)`. Whether excluding those is correct product behavior isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but the finding is correct that a broader behavior change was introduced alongside caching work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race/lost-update in the 'search key not yet cached' branch: concurrent requests with different organizationIds can both append their own search key and the second addRevisioned overwrites the first, leaving one org's results absent from the cache; also unbounded chained-query growth per distinct orgId

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, when a cache entry exists but `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` is null, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then writes a *new* `IdentityProviderListQuery` back with `cache.addRevisioned(query, ...)` (constructed as `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`). This is a non-atomic read/modify/write on a single `cacheKey` shared by all orgIds for the same `FetchMode`, so concurrent requests for different `organizationId` values can plausibly race and the last `addRevisioned` wins, losing the other org’s newly-added searchKey in the cached structure. Also, repeatedly creating `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)` suggests a chained/linked structure that can grow with each distinct `searchKey` (orgId), which is an unbounded cache-entry growth/perf concern visible from the diff, even if it doesn’t change correctness of returned results (it falls back to delegate on miss).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale-by-ID resolution only repairs the local node via registerInvalidation; other cluster nodes keep stale cache entries and hit the same fallback every request or serve removed/disabled providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that when a cached ID in getForLogin() resolves to null, it calls realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey) and falls back to the delegate. However, nothing in the diff indicates whether registerInvalidation propagates cluster-wide or is local-only. The finding’s assertion about other cluster nodes keeping stale entries (and repeatedly serving stale/removed/disabled providers) depends on cache/invalidation implementation details not present in the diff, so it’s not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE risk in new predicate: idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) throws NPE if getConfig() returns null

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` to `getLoginPredicate()`. While this would NPE *if* `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` could return null, the diff does not show that `getConfig()` is nullable or any call sites where it is null. Therefore the claimed NPE risk cannot be verified from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin uses wrong alias 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i (and 'idp-alias-20'), making cleanup a no-op with potential NPE; idp-alias-1 removed mid-test without cleanup tracking and 20 IDPs leak into subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (same mistake repeated for `idp-alias-20`). This does not match the created aliases shown in the diff, so cleanup will not remove the created IDPs (and may even fail at cleanup time if alias "alias" doesn't exist). Additionally, `idp-alias-1` is removed mid-test but no correct cleanup entry exists for it either due to the same wrong alias usage, so the created IDPs can leak into subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) even when a valid cache entry already contains the internalId, causing a redundant storage round trip on every IDP removal

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff adds `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the cache-validity check. This means a delegate/storage lookup happens unconditionally, even in the `else` branch where a valid cache entry may already provide the internalId (via `CachedIdentityProvider cached = realmCache.getCache().get(...)`). That introduces a redundant round trip on every removal for the purpose of later `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` / `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. This is a concrete performance/efficiency regression, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.
